definitions.explanation: To catch one's foot on something and lose balance while walking or running. The obstacle causes an unintended forward motion that may or may not result in a fall.

definitions.gloss: to encounter an obstacle; to hit a snag
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, to encounter an unexpected problem or difficulty that hinders progress in work, life, or a project.

examples.japanese: {石|いし}につまずいて{転|ころ}んだ。
examples.english: I tripped on a stone and fell.

examples.japanese: {暗|くら}い{廊下|ろうか}でつまずかないように{気|き}をつけてください。
examples.english: Please be careful not to trip in the dark hallway.

examples.japanese: {段差|だんさ}につまずいて{足首|あしくび}をひねってしまった。
examples.english: I tripped on a step and twisted my ankle.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいプロジェクトは{予算|よさん}{問題|もんだい}でつまずいた。
examples.english: The new project hit a snag due to budget issues.

examples.japanese: {出|で}だしからつまずいてしまった。
examples.english: I stumbled right from the start.

examples.japanese: {受験勉強|じゅけんべんきょう}で{数学|すうがく}につまずいて、{塾|じゅく}に{通|かよ}い{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: I was struggling with math in my exam prep, so I started going to a cram school.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
・つまずく → つまずかない (negative)
・つまずく → つまずいて (te-form)
・つまずく → つまずいた (past)

ORTHOGRAPHY:
Can be written in kanji as {躓|つまず}く, but the hiragana form is more common in everyday writing.

USAGE:
The physical meaning (sense 1) is more common in everyday conversation, while the figurative meaning (sense 2) appears frequently in news and business contexts.

COLLOCATIONS:
・{石|いし}につまずく - to trip on a stone
・{段差|だんさ}につまずく - to trip on a step
・{最初|さいしょ}の{一歩|いっぽ}でつまずく - to stumble at the first step
・{出|で}だしからつまずく - to stumble from the start
